mechanism_narrative: A continued rebound in WORKPLACES mobility restores weekday foot traffic and nearby discretionary spending, so RETAIL_REC should rise relative to the prior four weeks over the next month.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays flat or rises while RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls while GROCERY_PHARM stays weak, households are spending more time outside home and making more errand-linked trips, which lifts RETAIL_REC within one week through convenience shopping and incidental purchases.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL drops below the prior week while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -15
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL declines and GROCERY_PHARM remains weak but RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp fall in TRANSIT mobility signals reduced access to shopping districts and fewer pass-by purchases, so RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next two weeks when transit demand breaks below its recent range.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week from an already negative level
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops further but RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility diverts discretionary time toward outdoor recreation and away from indoor retail, causing RETAIL_REC to soften over the following four weeks when park visits remain elevated.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above its prior two-week average for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS stays elevated but RETAIL_REC does not decline versus the prior four weeks over the next month, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover together, commuting combines with in-person activity and increases opportunistic shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks more than either series would imply alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT strengthen but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under restrictions, any further reduction in TRANSIT mobility compresses access to malls and dining corridors, producing a near-term drop in RETAIL_REC within one week of the transit break.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT is below -45 and declines again week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is below -45 and falls further but RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the next week, the hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rebound in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL signals more localized routine trips and neighborhood errand clustering, which should support retail visits over the next two weeks even without major changes in commuting.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A strong PARKS surge combined with weak TRANSIT indicates outdoor substitution and lower downtown access, so RETAIL_REC should underperform over the next four weeks when both patterns persist together.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above +20 while TRANSIT stays below -40
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated and TRANSIT remains depressed but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior four weeks over the next month, the hypothesis fails.
